description: This line plot illustrates the relative change in performance (likely accuracy or efficiency) across different transformer layer groups when applying various key-value (KV) cache compression strategies, compared to a 4-bit baseline. The x-axis represents five grouped layer ranges: “Layer1-4”, “Layer5-12”, “Layer13-20”, “Layer21-28”, and “Layer29-32”, indicating a progression through the model’s depth. The y-axis, labeled “Relative Change”, is scaled from -25% to +5% in 5% increments, showing how each compression method deviates from the baseline. Five distinct lines are plotted: “LB-Avg of 2×tokens,8-bit” (gold with circle markers, solid line) remains near 0% across all layers; “LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit” (red with square markers, solid line) starts near 0%, dips to about -5% at Layer5-12, recovers to 0% at Layer13-20, then stays near 0%; “RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit” (teal with circle markers, solid line) begins at ~-2%, drops to ~-14% at Layer13-20, then recovers to ~-2% by Layer29-32; “RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit” (dark blue with square markers, solid line) starts at ~-4%, plunges to -25% at Layer13-20, then rebounds to ~-4% at Layer29-32; and the “Baseline of 4×tokens,4-bit” (gray dashed line) is fixed at 0% across all layers, serving as the reference point. The plot visually demonstrates that compression methods using fewer tokens and higher bit-widths (e.g., 1×tokens,16-bit) suffer larger performance drops in middle layers, while methods using more tokens and lower bit-widths (e.g., 2×tokens,8-bit) maintain more stable performance.
